subject: Re: Load test coordination & SLO verification — next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finwise.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Load test coordination & SLO verification — next steps

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled and validate the performance SLOs you outlined.

Recap of requirements you shared:
- Target SLOs: p95 end-to-end latency <= 200ms for short text generation (<= 256 tokens); p99 < 400ms. For streaming chat flows we need token-level latency <= 25ms per chunk.
- Target throughput / concurrency: sustained 1,200 req/s with bursts to 2,500 req/s; concurrency target 200-300 simultaneous sessions.
- Test duration / window: preferred 2-hour sustained run + a 30m ramp. You suggested daytime slot next week.
- Metrics of interest: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate (4xx/5xx), throughput (tokens/sec), stream fragmentation/drop rate, CPU/GPU utilization.
- Model variants: prod model (redwood/gptx-2.1) + a quantized variant for cost comparison.

What we (Redwood) need from FinWise to proceed:
1) Confirm a firm test window (we suggested Tue 2027-03-29 16:00-18:30 PT; alternate Wed 2027-03-30 09:00-11:30 PT).
2) Provide the IPs/ranges to allowlist on your side (we will provide our egress list).
3) Test account or API key you want us to use for generating traffic (or confirm you will drive the k6 load from your env).
4) Typical payload shapes (average token lengths, top-k/temperature settings) and any non-standard headers we should send.

Attachments I'll send in a follow-up from our side: k6 script (k6_script_v2.js), loadtest runbook (loadtest_runbook.pdf), and a suggested IP allowlist file (ip_allowlist.txt).

Next steps: if you can confirm the window and whether you want Redwood to originate the load or if FinWise will run the k6 scripts, we'll finalize the runbook and credentials. Marissa (cc'd) will provision a test account and a short-lived API key once we confirm the window.

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

— Logan

Hi Logan / Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side:

- The targets look right to us; p95 <= 200ms and p99 < 400ms are what we need to validate for prod workloads. Streaming token latency target is important — we rely on sub-30ms per-chunk delivery.
- We'd prefer Redwood to originate the traffic for the first run so we can observe from our edge and simplify firewall setup. If that works, please provide the source IPs we should allowlist.
- Preferred window: Wed 2027-03-30 09:00-11:30 PT (Tom and our infra team are available then). If Redwood can do Tue 3/29 we can adjust but Wed is preferred.
- We'll need a short-lived test account for instrumentation with a scoped API key and a hostname allowlist on your side (we'll open our side too).
- Payload shapes: typical prompts are 40-120 tokens; occasional long prompts up to 800 tokens for document summarization. We'll attach a sample corpus (sensitive data redacted).

Cc'ing Security Ops — please advise if you need our SOC2 report or any signing authority for the test keys.

If you can send the k6 script and runbook, we will validate internally and confirm the window.

Best,
Alice Chen
Sr. SRE, FinWise

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks — Wed 2027-03-30 09:00-11:30 PT works for Redwood. Per Logan's note, I've attached the artifacts and stubbed credentials:

Attachments:
- k6_script_v2.js (k6 script configured for streaming SSE + long-tail prompt mix)
- loadtest_runbook.pdf (step-by-step runbook, metrics collection checklist)
- ip_allowlist.txt (our egress ranges to allow on FinWise firewall)

Quick notes from the runbook and what we'll measure:
- Run profile: 30m ramp to 1,200 rps, 2hr sustained at 1,200 rps, 30m step-burst up to 2,500 rps for 10m, then cool-down.
- Concurrency: k6 virtual users simulate ~220 concurrent sessions with realistic think times and streaming chunking.
- Streaming: we emulate token-chunked SSE with 64-token chunks; we report chunk latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) and reassembly errors.
- Telemetry: please ensure your edge exports request_id and trace headers (x-request-id, traceparent). We'll include these in the script so you can correlate traces.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, 4xx/5xx counts, stream-drop %, GPU utilization, and memory consumption on the host.

Test credentials / provisioning steps:
- We will create a scoped test API key for FinWise: FINWISE-TEST-20270330 (will be active only for the window). For security we will provide the key via the secure vault link in the runbook (not in email).
- If FinWise wants to originate traffic, we can provide the same k6 script and a short checklist to run from your environment.

IP allowlist (high-level):
- 35.198.72.0/24
- 35.199.16.0/20
(Full list included in ip_allowlist.txt attachment)

Operational support:
- We'll have on-call infra + an SRE (Rishi, cc'd) in the run channel during the window. For urgent issues call Redwood Ops: +1 (415) 555-0199.

Let us know if you need any changes. If SecurityOps needs a signed NDA or SOC2 evidence we can surface that as well.

— Marissa
